items.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
items.snippet: The FBI is warning that hackers are using an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against organizations worldwide, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments. [...]
items.summary: The FBI warns that hackers are using ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration testing framework, to automate attacks, including a ConnectWise supply-chain breach affecting Microsoft 365 customer environments.
items.why: Check exposure to ConnectWise and review Microsoft 365 environments for signs of compromise.

items.title: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
items.snippet: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) confirmed that personal employee data has been leaked online after a threat actor put 6.9GB of information allegedly stolen from the company up for auction. [...]
items.summary: TSMC confirmed that personal employee data was leaked online after a threat actor offered information allegedly stolen from the company for auction.
items.why: Review employee-data exposure and monitor for misuse of leaked personal information.

items.title: Pentagon Renames CDAO ‘Super Intelligence Office’
items.snippet: The move follows President Trump’s order to replace “artificial intelligence” with “super intelligence” in executive branch communications. The post Pentagon Renames CDAO ‘Super Intelligence Office’ appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: SecurityWeek reports that the Pentagon renamed CDAO the “Super Intelligence Office,” following an order to replace “artificial intelligence” in executive branch communications.
items.why: The name change reflects how the office and its remit are presented.

items.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
items.snippet: Meta was fined €805 million in Italy yesterday over a Facebook for Android feature that suggests photos and videos from users' phone galleries for them to post. The Garante, Italy's data protection authority, found that the feature was enabled by default and that the app accessed Italian users' photos, videos, and rela
items.summary: Meta was fined €805 million in Italy over a Facebook for Android feature that suggests gallery photos and videos for posting. Italy’s data protection authority found the feature was enabled by default.
items.why: Review whether apps access device galleries by default and whether users give informed consent.

items.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
items.snippet: The compromise of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on Cursor's extension marketplace was the result of the theft of an access key that was exposed in the wake of a breach targeting Fireworks AI. "An attacker obtained an access key we had issued to Fireworks," Cursor said in a Friday update. "The key was expos
items.summary: Cursor says a stolen access key, exposed after a breach targeting Fireworks AI, led to the compromise of Anthropic’s official Claude Code extension on Cursor’s marketplace.
items.why: Check exposed or third-party access keys, and verify extensions before installing or distributing them.

items.summary: Help Net Security’s roundup highlights stories including a secret stealer hitting GitHub repositories and Claude Code becoming a remote-controlled implant.
items.why: Review repository secrets and investigate unexpected remote-control behavior in developer tools.

items.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
items.snippet: Cursor confirmed it suffered a security breach that let hackers distribute a malicious Claude Code extension through its marketplace after stealing credentials from AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI. [...]
items.summary: Cursor confirmed a security breach that let hackers distribute a malicious Claude Code extension through its marketplace after stealing credentials from AI infrastructure provider Firework.
items.why: Review marketplace extensions and credentials associated with AI infrastructure providers.

items.title: US disrupts North Korean campaign behind $400 million crypto theft
items.snippet: The U.S. government has disrupted a North Korean social engineering campaign called 'FaceStealer', responsible for stealing more than $400 million in cryptocurrency. [...]
items.summary: The U.S. government says it disrupted North Korea’s FaceStealer social engineering campaign, which it says was responsible for stealing more than $400 million in cryptocurrency.
items.why: Check for social engineering attempts and reinforce controls around cryptocurrency access.

items.title: Meta Fined $887 Million in Italy Over Android Gallery Photos and Videos on Facebook
items.snippet: The directive protects smartphones as part of a person’s private sphere and requires “free and informed consent” for such access, the authority said. The post Meta Fined $887 Million in Italy Over Android Gallery Photos and Videos on Facebook appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: SecurityWeek reports that Meta was fined $887 million in Italy over Facebook’s access to Android gallery photos and videos. The authority said access requires free and informed consent.
items.why: Check whether mobile apps access private media only with users’ free and informed consent.

items.title: Is AI Making Us Worse at Cybersecurity?
items.snippet: Overreliance on AI could erode the creativity, clear communication, and critical thinking security teams need when there’s no playbook. The post Is AI Making Us Worse at Cybersecurity? appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: The article warns that overreliance on AI could weaken security teams’ creativity, communication, and critical thinking when no playbook exists.
items.why: Keep human review and clear incident communication in security workflows that use AI.

items.title: Royal Navy submariners welcomed home after deterrent patrol keeping UK safe
items.snippet: Royal Navy submariners have returned home to their families following another successful patrol protecting the UK and our allies through Britain's nuclear deterrent.
items.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence says Royal Navy submariners returned home after a patrol supporting Britain's nuclear deterrent.
items.why: The patrol illustrates the operational role of the UK's nuclear deterrent.

items.title: Malaysia Selects Roketsan’s ATMACA to Replace NSM on Littoral Combat Ships
items.snippet: Malaysia picks Roketsan’s ATMACA anti-ship missile to replace Kongsberg’s NSM on its LCS vessels, with French SETIS CMS integration still unresolved. The post Malaysia Selects Roketsan’s ATMACA to Replace NSM on Littoral Combat Ships appeared first on Naval News .
items.summary: Malaysia picked Roketsan’s ATMACA anti-ship missile to replace Kongsberg’s NSM on its littoral combat ships. Integration with the French SETIS combat management system remains unresolved.
items.why: The missile replacement and unresolved combat-system integration are relevant to ship capability and procurement.

items.title: Naval Group Unveils SCX 26 ‘Hybrid Fleet’ Drone Mothership Concept
items.snippet: French shipbuilder Naval Group unveiled a new conceptual surface warship design at Euronaval 2026 dubbed “SCX 26.” Naval News provides an overview covering the key technical characteristics and wider operational concept, explaining how SCX 26 fits into the company’s vision for the future of naval warfare. Standing for
items.summary: Naval Group unveiled the SCX 26, a conceptual surface warship design described as a “Hybrid Fleet” drone mothership.
items.why: The concept highlights the operational role of a surface warship designed around drones.

items.title: Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink restrictions and be on 'right side of history'
items.snippet: The Ukrainian president says restrictions are still in place and making it difficult to stop Russian attacks.
items.summary: Zelensky says Starlink restrictions remain in place and make it difficult to stop Russian attacks; he urges the US and Musk to lift them.
items.why: The restrictions highlight the strategic role of satellite connectivity in Ukraine's ability to respond to attacks.

items.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
items.snippet: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.
items.summary: Megaspeed says a suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's former boss left in 2025. The scandal has raised questions about whether advanced AI chips reached China despite US restrictions.
items.why: The report raises questions about advanced-chip access and the reach of US restrictions.

items.title: How telecoms upgrade work sparked US flight chaos
items.snippet: US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading and not a cyber-attack.
items.summary: US officials say old equipment overload caused the ground stop, not a cyber-attack.
items.why: The account highlights how equipment overload can disrupt air travel without a cyber-attack.

items.title: Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
items.snippet: It marks the second attack on the country in three days and comes as the US and Iran remain locked in a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz.
items.summary: The report says Iran targeted a US military base in Bahrain with a drone attack, amid a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz.
items.why: The reported attack connects drone operations with tensions around the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Prince Harry in Ukraine meeting Invictus 2027 hopefuls
items.snippet: British royal says he's 'taken a risk' in his fourth surprise visit to Ukraine since 2022 to meet wounded veterans.
items.summary: Al Jazeera reports that Prince Harry visited Ukraine to meet wounded veterans and Invictus 2027 hopefuls.
items.why: The visit places wounded veterans and Ukraine's ongoing conflict in focus.

items.title: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker
items.snippet: Eight arrests made in connection with an attempted arson, which Tallinn says was ordered by Russian intelligence.
items.summary: Estonia says it will close border crossings with Russia after an attempted arson attack on a drone maker; Tallinn says Russian intelligence ordered it.
items.why: The reported incident links border policy to security concerns around a drone maker.

items.title: Yemeni government forces redeploy from Bab al-Mandeb to defend Aden
items.snippet: Spokesman for the Southern Armed Forces says group is repositioning from Dhubab airport and areas around Bab al-Mandeb.
items.summary: A spokesman for the Southern Armed Forces says Yemeni government forces are repositioning from areas around Bab al-Mandeb to defend Aden.
items.why: The reported redeployment shifts forces between the Bab al-Mandeb area and Aden.

items.title: 70 bodies recovered from Gaza rubble, thousands still missing
items.snippet: 70 bodies recovered from Gaza rubble, thousands still missing
items.summary: Al Jazeera reports that 70 bodies have been recovered from Gaza rubble, while thousands remain missing.
items.why: The report indicates the continuing human toll and uncertainty around missing people in Gaza.

learn.explainer: A supply-chain breach involves an attack connected to a supplier or service used by other organizations. The FBI warning describes a ConnectWise breach that affected Microsoft 365 customer environments.

A nuclear deterrent is a military capability intended to discourage attacks by making the prospect of a nuclear response part of an adversary's calculations. The UK Ministry of Defence says the patrol supported Britain's deterrent.
The Strait of Hormuz is a geographic feature named in the report as the focus of a stand-off involving the US and Iran. The item places an Iranian drone attack in Bahrain alongside those tensions.

analysis.headline: Connectivity, access and pressure across security domains
paragraphs: The Starlink dispute and questions about advanced AI chips reaching China despite US restrictions also center on who can use critical capabilities. These reports suggest that defenders and analysts should distinguish confirmed statements from allegations, and track how access, restrictions and third-party dependencies shape risk.

The Iran drone report and the reported movement of Yemeni forces add operational and geographic context, while the UK describes a submarine patrol supporting its nuclear deterrent. A separate report attributes US flight disruption to old equipment overloading, not a cyber-attack. Watch how officials describe causes and constraints; the available snippets do not establish broader links.
takeaways: Review third-party exposure and access to sensitive environments.
Separate confirmed facts from claims and unresolved questions.
Track how infrastructure restrictions affect operational options.
